idiom_name: nested functions over the enclosing function's variables; private struct with mutating funcs as the escalation
implementation_notes: Nested functions are closures: they can capture and modify the enclosing function's arguments, constants and variables, and Swift manages the memory (Swift book, Functions and Closures). The steps therefore share the frame without any type. If a nested function escapes - returned or stored - Swift moves the captured variables to the heap and keeps them alive by reference, so the returned computation becomes a stateful object in its own right; a private struct with mutating funcs is the explicit form when the algorithm must be tested, reused or given multiple entry points.
pitfalls: Escaping nested functions capture by reference and are heap-boxed; a stored nested function that captures self strongly can create a retain cycle.
A nested function cannot capture an inout parameter and escape, and inout parameters may not be captured by escaping closures at all.
Because capture is by reference, every step observes later mutations of the captured variables - usually intended, but surprising when a step is invoked out of order.
